summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic heart failure, and a history of gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted with fever, cough, and hypoxia. He was transferred from a rehab facility where he had been recovering from a prior admission for hip pain. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis, elevated BNP, and chest imaging showing pulmonary edema and worsening opacities concerning for healthcare-associated pneumonia. He was treated with vancomycin and cefepime, later transitioned to ceftazidime for dialysis compatibility. His infection markers improved, oxygen was weaned off, and he was stabilized on his baseline heart failure and diabetes regimens. Cinacalcet was held due to low calcium. A stage II coccygeal pressure ulcer was monitored without intervention. He completed a dialysis session prior to discharge and was transitioned back to extended care with plans to complete a seven-day antibiotic course. He was alert, ambulatory with assistance, and clinically improved at discharge.
